title: PLGA Nanoparticles Formed by Single- or Double-emulsion with Vitamin E-TPGS
protocol: Weigh 100 mg (+/- 5 mg) of PLGA and place in a test tube.
Transfer 1 ml solvent (ethyl acetate or dichloromethane) to the sample with a glass serological pipette.
Cover the top of the tube with a small piece of aluminum foil.
Parafilm the foil securely, wrapping tightly across the top edge of the vial and bottom edge of the foil.
Mark the level of the solvent on the outside of the test tube.
Let the polymer dissolve overnight, adding additional solvent if evaporation occurs.
Vortex on high until all polymer is completely dissolved (~10 min) if preparing nanoparticles the day of use.
Prepare a work area in the fume hood with the following equipment/materials: vortexer, two small glass Pasteur pipettes with rubber bulbs, and a magnetic stir plate.
Place a large beaker full of ice water on a stand below the ultrasonicator.
Add 45 ml of 0.3% w/v Vitamin E-TPGS to a 200 ml glass beaker with a magnetic stir bar and set stirring speed to 360 rpm.
Add 2 ml of 0.3% w/v Vitamin E-TPGS to a 13 mm x 100 mm glass test tube.
Add encapsulant directly to the polymer solution and vortex until homogenously dispersed for hydrophobic agents.
Emulsify encapsulant with the polymer solution before proceeding for hydrophilic agents.
Add up to 50 μl of drug in water or buffer to the surface of the polymer solution.
Ultrasonicate briefly on ice to emulsify the drug with polymer (typically 10 sec).
Place the open tube containing polymer/encapsulant near the vortexer.
Hold the test tube containing Vitamin E-TPGS vertically and on high vortex.
Use a glass Pasteur pipette to add the polymer/encapsulant solution dropwise, avoiding the sides of the tube.
Drop the polymer solution directly onto the surface of the vortexing emulsifier.
Continue vortexing the solution (now an emulsion) for an additional 15 sec after adding the entire 1 ml of polymer solution.
Transfer the emulsified polymer to the ultrasonicator.
Immerse the test tube containing the emulsion in ice water.
Sonicate the emulsion in three 10 sec bursts at 40% amplitude.
Move the emulsion up and down the probe during sonication.
Pause between each ten second sonication to cool the solution.
Add 1-2 ml of 0.3% Vitamin E-TPGS to the emulsion using a glass Pasteur pipette.
Empty the emulsion into the stirring solution.
Repeat the step to wash out any remaining solution from the test tube.
Stir nanoparticles for three hours while allowing solvent evaporation.
If encapsulant is light-sensitive, wrap the beaker in aluminum foil with the top open.
Split hardened nanoparticles into two Oak Ridge centrifuge tubes.
Balance the centrifuge tubes to within 0.1 g.
Centrifuge nanoparticles at 17,000 x g for 15 min in a fixed-angle rotor.
Discard the supernatant without disturbing the nanoparticle pellet.
Add 15 ml diH2O to resuspend nanoparticles using a water bath sonicator or vortexer.
Combine contents of two centrifuge tubes into one tube.
Repeat steps 2.1-2.3 two more times for a total of three washes in 30 ml diH2O each time.
Resuspend the final pellet in 4-5 ml fluid volume.
Add a weight ratio of 1:2 trehalose to polymer as a cryoprotectant.
Freeze an aliquot without trehalose for SEM imaging.
Transfer nanoparticles to a preweighed 5 ml centrifuge tube and freeze at -80 °C for at least 30 min.
If any melting occurs, refreeze before placing in the lyophilizer.
Lyophilize for 72 hours for a 5 ml volume.
Store lyophilized particles in a Parafilm-wrapped tube at -80 °C.
Place a strip of double-sided carbon tape on an SEM stub.
Label the metal portion of the stub using permanent marker for later reference.
Use a metal spatula to collect a small quantity of lyophilized nanoparticles and gently spread them across the surface of the tape.
Brush the surface of the stub with a lab tissue or use compressed air to remove loose nanoparticles.
Sputter coat the sample with gold-paladium for 30-120 seconds.
Set typical parameters for visualizing particles as a working distance of 5-15 mm, beam strength of 5-12 kV, and a spot size of 1-3.
Observe microparticles at 100X magnification.
Distinguish nanoparticles at 3,000X magnification.
Focus on the edge of a flake where it meets tape or the top of a sphere to locate easily visualized particles.
Collect at least three images per batch.
